User: an agent told me this: The ruthless collapse is **not** “invent one generic read/session API.” That was already rejected for good reason. The collapse should be:

> **One public model: concept-owned active reads. Everything else is private machinery.**

A concept-owned active read is already defined in #2508: a kept-live query with a close handle; it opens demand, replays cache/store, pushes typed output while mounted, then closes exact demand. The same issue explicitly says “session” is runtime bookkeeping, not a public noun, and rejects `open_session(namespace, bytes)`. [...] Use only these public words:

```text id="ghcb2h"
open_<concept>(spec/target) -> Handle
close(handle)
load_more(handle)          // only where paging is intrinsic, e.g. feeds/search
typed output               // what the host renders
```

Everything else becomes internal. [...] | Current word          |                                Fate | Replacement                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------: | --------------------------------------- |
| **active read**       |           keep as architecture noun | concept-owned active read               |
| **typed session**     |      mostly delete from public docs | active read / `open_<concept>`          |
| **feed session**      |               delete as public noun | feed read / `open_feed`                 |
| **observed delivery** |                        private only | event delivery inside read runtime      |
| **projection**        | private-ish; public docs say output | typed output / snapshot output          |
| **source reducer**    |                        private only | source resolution inside the read owner |
| **Trellis**           |                        private only | not mentioned in NMP app API            | [...] Collapse the internals into **one read lifecycle engine** with three stages.

```text id="bbtljm"
ConceptRead
  1. Demand
     What events/resources must be alive?

  2. Admission + model
     Which matching facts matter, and how do they update state?

  3. Output
     What typed data is emitted to the host?
```

That lets the implementation contain source reducers, observed sinks, projections, Trellis graphs, reverse indexes, etc., without teaching any of those nouns to app authors. [...] A concept owner supplies:

```rust id="bo3hwa"
trait ConceptRead {
    type Spec;
    type Handle;
    type Output;

    fn open(spec: Self::Spec) -> Self::Handle;
    fn close(handle: Self::Handle);

    // Internal, not app-facing:
    // - compile demand
    // - replay cached/stored rows
    // - subscribe live
    // - admit/filter events
    // - maintain bounded model
    // - emit typed output
    // - tombstone/clear on close/account switch
}
```

Do **not** expose this as a universal public trait unless there is a concrete reason. It can be an internal pattern plus a few narrow registrar traits. [...] ## The brutal version

NMP should have **one read abstraction**, but **many concept APIs**.

Not:

```text id="e2jibv"
one generic read API + many opaque namespaces
```

Instead:

```text id="88cd4g"
one lifecycle model + many explicit owners
```

That is the distinction agents will keep missing unless the repo deletes the seductive intermediate nouns. [...] User: The other agent is right. I’d amend my answer. My previous “delete or deprecate” and “code can keep internal names temporarily” were too soft for this repo.

## Corrected position

The collapse should be:

```text id="0vjq6y"
One lifecycle engine.
Many explicit concept-owned public APIs.
No deprecated public side doors.
No generic namespace/session doorway.
No public observed/projection/source-reducer vocabulary.
No post-v1 rename debt.
```

The current code still violates that direction: `NmpApp::open_observed_feed_source` is a public method, marked `#[deprecated]`, but its doc comment still says it “remains the correct doorway” when a caller needs a raw `ObservedProjectionSink` hook. That is not deletion; it is a blessed escape hatch with a warning label.

That conflicts with the repo’s own API doctrine: public surfaces are cleaned in place before v1, and NMP does not retain pre-v1 compatibility shims, dead parameters, deprecated schema slots, or old paths solely to protect callers.

## What should change in the memo

Replace this:

```text id="d2l542"
delete or deprecate open_observed_feed_source
```

with this:

```text id="t2vnx6"
Delete open_observed_feed_source as a public NmpApp method.
Update every caller in the same PR.
If one consumer still needs app-owned row projection over NMP feed acquisition, express it as a named concept-owned read or app-owned recipe, not a public raw ObservedProjectionSink doorway. [...] ```text id="18rm0d"
Internal names may survive only behind private modules and explicit doctrine-lint ratchets.
No public docs, generated helpers, templates, examples, or pub API items may expose session/ObservedProjection/ReducedSource/open_interest/Trellis vocabulary unless the file is explicitly internal-runtime documentation. [...] ```text id="if4v3l"
Delete as public API:
- open_observed_feed_source
- open_interest, if still reachable from product/app surfaces
- raw observer/projection lifecycle APIs
- generic session namespace doors
- relation bucket APIs
- app-visible ReducedSource / ObservedProjection nouns [...] ```text id="qu1vk2"
A read is opened through an explicit concept-owned API, executed by one shared internal lifecycle engine, and rendered from typed output. Apps never assemble interests, observers, projections, source reducers, generic sessions, or Trellis resources.
``` [...] One note on it: I DONT WANT ANY DEPRECATION/BACKWARDS-COMPAT ANYWHERE -- deprecated code is to be REMOVED [...] #2453 had the right audit framing: every surviving app-visible read door should be classified as typed helper, internal/private executor, transitional with owner issue, or stale/violating. That audit discipline should become a permanent ratchet.
